question: Sapna invested ₹22,800 on simple interest, partly at 5% per annum and partly at 11% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 4 years, then find the sum invested at 5% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When Simple Interest is equal for two parts over the same time period, the ratio of principal amounts is P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁.

Ratio of sum invested at 5% to 11% = 11 : 5

Total parts = 11 + 5 = 16 parts ⇒ 16 parts = ₹22,800

1 part = 22,800 ÷ 16 = ₹1,425

Sum invested at 5% (11 parts) = 11 × 1,425 = ₹15,675

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,675.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Investment = ₹22,800

Rate 1 (R₁) = 5% p.a., Rate 2 (R₂) = 11% p.a.

Time (T) = 4 years for both investments.

Simple Interest earned from both parts is equal.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
